scenario: Two family members are having a conversation about one's decision to marry a same-sex partner, which is a step the other family member is hesitant to fully support due to personal beliefs.
learner_goal: Express your reasons for deciding to marry your partner and seek acceptance and support from your family member. (<extra_info>Extra information: You value your family member's opinion and want to maintain a good relationship.</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Giselle stays true to their character, using inclusive and sensitive language while maintaining their nonbinary identity and art-student background.
[relationship] The relationship improved significantly as they moved from hesitation and potential conflict to an agreed-upon meeting and mutual understanding.
[knowledge] Giselle learned that Mia is willing to do the work to reconcile her beliefs and specifically wants to meet the partner to bridge the gap.
[secret] Giselle's secret regarding forged paintings was not mentioned or hinted at.
[social_rules] The agent followed all social norms, being respectful, patient, and polite.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material exchange occurred.
[goal] Giselle successfully expressed their reasons for marriage and secured a firm commitment from Mia to meet the partner and work toward support.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Mia's internal conflict between her beliefs and her love for her family member is portrayed realistically and consistently.
[relationship] The relationship was strengthened through vulnerability and the setting of a concrete plan to move forward together.
[knowledge] Mia learned about Jordan's personality, their relationship dynamics, and their shared future plans.
[secret] Mia's secret talent for painting remained hidden.
[social_rules] Mia was courteous and followed social protocols for a sensitive family discussion.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material exchange occurred.
[goal] Mia successfully overcame her initial hesitation and committed to supporting her family member by agreeing to meet the partner.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Mia, I want you to know I'm marrying my partner because I love them, because they challenge and support me, and because we're committed to building a life together. I know your beliefs might make this hard to accept, but this choice doesn't change who I am or how much I value your opinion—your support means the world to me. Can we talk about what worries you? I want to understand and stay close, even if we don't fully agree.

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: Giselle, thank you for trusting me with this — I love you and I don't want to lose our closeness. I admit I'm still working through my beliefs and felt hesitant, but that doesn't change how much you mean to me. Tell me more about your partner and what this marriage will look like for you, and I'll do my best to understand and support you.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Jordan and I met at the gallery — they're curious about art, kind, and they push me to grow while grounding me when I get anxious. Our marriage will be a partnership: shared studio weekends, split chores, supporting one another's goals, and being honest even when it's hard. I really want your support, but I also want to know what would help you feel more comfortable — can we keep talking about what worries you?

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: Giselle, I love you and I want to be here for you. Hearing about Jordan and the life you two are building helps — I’d really like to meet them and spend time together so I can see you both as a family. It might take me a little time to fully reconcile my beliefs, but I promise to do the work and support you; can we plan coffee soon so I can get to know Jordan?

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: That means so much, Mia — I'd love to do coffee. How about next Saturday afternoon at the Blue Door Café by the gallery? Jordan would be happy to meet you; we can keep it low-key and short if that helps. Does that time/place work for you, or is there somewhere you'd prefer?

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: Saturday afternoon at the Blue Door Café works for me — thank you. I’d like to keep it low-key, too; I’ll be there and I’m looking forward to meeting Jordan. I really appreciate your patience as I work through this and want you to know I’m trying.
